subject: Volume-indexed holdback and price shelf — commercialization scenarios
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Draft — volume-indexed holdback and price-shelf scenarios for Stellara RFP

Team,

Attached are three commercial scenarios to include in our RFP response to Stellara. High-level notes below — the spreadsheet has the token bands, unit pricing, and an automated reconciliation example.

Key concepts (short):
- Price shelf: tie baseline unit price for the first 12 months, then a pre-agreed indexed shelf for years 2–3 (floor and cap).
- Volume-indexed holdback: 7% of committed spend reserved monthly and released on quarterly reconciliation if actuals >= 90% of committed volume; early-release triggers for MRR conversion events.
- Burst cushion: 20% on top of committed throughput for the first 30 days of go-live without overage charges; after that burst is billed at tiered overage rates.
- Escrow mechanics: customer escrow for holdback funds (customer KYC + escrow agent). We drafted standard escrow clauses in the attached PDF.

Requests:
1) Marissa — please take scenario 2 and draft two short bullets we can put in the RFP (one-line impact on ARR, one-line capability statement).
2) Ben — confirm whether legal can accept the escrow agent list as-is; flag any major compliance blockers.
3) Priyom — sanity-check the invoicing cadence and true-up table (sheet: reconciliation_sample).

I'll incorporate into the commercial section tonight and send to Elena first thing Monday.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): 20271002_price_scenarios.xlsx (xlsx), escrow_terms_draft.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Re: Draft — volume-indexed holdback and price-shelf scenarios for Stellara RFP

Karthik — taking scenario 2. Two bullets for the RFP: 

- Commercial impact: Anchoring first-year unit price with a capped indexed shelf reduces headline ARR risk while giving Stellara predictable per-token economics (expected reduction in invoice volatility by ~18%).
- Operational note: Our reconciliation automation compares monthly aggregated token usage against the committed band and releases holdback quarterly; minimal billing ops overhead — we provide reconciliation CSV + audit trace.

Ben — any flags on the escrow agent list? If legal wants alternate language I can add an explanatory footnote in the RFP (we prefer escrow only when customers request additional purchase protection).

I'll fold these into the RFP excerpt and run a quick proof with marketing for tone.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morris <elena@stellara.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@stellara.io
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood RFP — clarifications on holdback and invoice flow

Karthik — thanks for the early draft. A few clarifying questions from procurement and finance: 

1) Release triggers: can you confirm whether the 90% threshold is based on committed token count or committed USD spend? We prefer spend-based.
2) If actuals are below 90% at quarter-end, is the holdback forfeited or applied as credit to future invoices? Our preference is credit to next invoice with a 12-month expiry.
3) Invoicing cadence: can we get monthly invoices with quarterly true-ups rather than quarterly invoices? That helps our bookkeeping.

Separately — we would like the price-shelf to include a CPI-based cap so we avoid large step-ups. Can you provide an example calculation for year 2 that shows a worst-case increase and a market-adjusted increase?

Also attaching the Raksha standard escrow addendum we usually require — it's not the same as the PDF you sent. Can your legal review?

Best,
Elena

--
Elena Morris
Procurement Lead
Stellara Inc.

[Attachment: Raksha_escrow_addendum_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@stellara.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood RFP — clarifications on holdback and invoice flow

Elena — really helpful questions. Below are concrete answers we can include in the RFP commercial appendix; copying internal owners for legal and billing follow-up.

1) Threshold basis: We can anchor the 90% threshold to committed USD spend (not token count). This maps cleanly to invoicing and is our recommended default for mixed-rate workloads.

2) Treatment when below threshold: Holdback is applied as credit to the next invoice and expires after 12 months if unused. If customer requests forfeiture as an alternative (rare), we can discuss, but standard approach is crediting to avoid contentious recovery flows.

3) Invoicing cadence: Monthly invoices + quarterly true-up is supported by our billing platform; the reconciliation sheet in the attachment shows a sample monthly invoice line and a quarterly true-up adjustment entry.

4) Price-shelf cap: We can implement a CPI-linked cap with a hard ceiling of +7% year-over-year. Example calculations (included inline in the spreadsheet):
   - Market-adjusted example: CPI + 1% -> result = +3.2% increase for year 2 (illustrative).
   - Worst-case cap applied: +7% (hard cap regardless of CPI).

5) Escrow addendum: Ben — can you confirm legal can accept Raksha's template or propose redlines (I highlighted the main clause differences in the PDF). If we need to propose an alternate escrow workflow (holdback on merchant account + audit log push), Priyom can map the reconciliation flow.

Next steps: Marissa and I will update the commercial appendix and push a clean PDF to procurement tomorrow. Priyom/Ben — can you aim for legal + billing comments by EOD Monday?

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround.

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
